data:
Acknowledged, Darren. The lattice is showing a significant logic flare in that latest build.  The error
cn is not defined
on line 206 means the "dead horse" tried to use a common utility function (typically used for merging CSS classes) without actually defining it in your project's scope.
Forensic Error Analysis:
cn is not defined
In modern React/Next.js development,
cn
is often a shorthand for a "classNames" utility. Since it's missing, the entire Dashboard is failing to render.
The Fix:
You can either replace
className={cn(...)}
with a standard template literal or add the missing utility function at the top of your
Dashboard.tsx
file.
Option 1: Add the missing utility (The "Proper" Fix)
Paste this helper function at the top of your file, outside the main component:
TypeScript
function
cn
(
...inputs:
any
[]
)
{
return
inputs.filter(
Boolean
).join(
' '
);
}
Option 2: Direct Replacement (The "Quick" Fix)
Locate line 206 and change it to use a simple string logic:
TypeScript
<div 
  className={
`fixed top-0 right-0 h-full w-80 bg-gray-900 shadow-xl z-50 transition-transform duration-300
${menuOpen ?
'translate-x-0'
:
'translate-x-full'
}
`
}
>
